name: Distinguishing Range
definition: Minimum number of coordinates over which all concepts in the class can be distinguished.
graph_summary: The largest coordinate set on which all concepts have distinct traces.

monotonic.proof: Any coordinate set that distinguishes all concepts of a class also distinguishes every subfamily. Minimizing its size therefore cannot increase after restricting the class.

p_monotonic.proof: Counterexample: H={0010,0011,0101,1000} has distinguishing range 2. A three-coordinate projection has trace {000,001,011,100}, whose four concepts require all three remaining coordinates to be distinguished. Thus the projected value is 3.

c_monotonic.proof: A coordinate set distinguishing a target in the original class remains distinguishing in a conditioned fibre after fixed coordinates are deleted.

doubly_monotonic.proof: By definition, doubly monotonicity requires both subfamily monotonicity and projection monotonicity; the recorded failure of one of them rules it out.

strictly_monotonic.proof: By definition, strictly monotonicity requires both doubly monotonicity and strict c-monotonicity; the recorded failure of one of them rules it out.
